newsitem.title: UK: UK consumer confidence set to grow further - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK consumer confidence set to grow further - survey.

text.p: Consumer confidence is running at its highest level yet in the 1990s and is set to be even higher by the UK general election, a new survey showed on Thursday.

Business Strategies Limited (BSL), an independent economics consultancy, said optimism about the economy and household finances was running at its highest level this decade, but it found the rate of improvement had eased slightly.
"Household finances are improving, with consumers in most regions expecting things to get better over the next year. But the rate of improvement has slowed," said David Fells, director at BSL.
The survey did not ask about the outlook for taxes, interest rates or the election, and was conducted before the quarter point rate rise on Wednesday.
Fells said these factors could be behind the slower growth of optimism. "People are expecting things to change and that could be responsible."

He said low inflation was partly behind the strong growth in high street spending, which is forecast to continue. The survey found consumers expect inflation to fall to around one percent in a year's time from 2.1 percent currently.

Optimism is running highest in Wales, Yorkshire and Humberside, London and Northern Ireland. "But the difference between the top and bottom regions is not great. Consumers are feeling good almost everywhere," said Fells.
Durable goods are set to be the main beneficiaries from the increasing confidence along with the more exotic areas of the leisure industry.

"The lump sum payments from (maturing tax-exempt savings) and building societies are more likely to be spent on big ticket items. And in terms of the leisure industry, spending will also be concentrated at the upper end -- the virtual reality centres rather than the bingo halls."
